user.title: Set up NetOrbit
user.description: Pick the network to map. NetOrbit pings devices on this subnet and reads Home Assistant's ARP table to learn their MAC addresses. Everything you set up is remembered by MAC address, so DHCP changing a device's IP is fine. For the tidiest map, give your router, switches and access points DHCP reservations.

data_description.subnet: In CIDR form, for example 10.0.0.0/24. Up to 1024 hosts.
data_description.gateway: Your router. It becomes the center of the map.
data_description.mode: Automatic tracks everything it finds. Manual only tracks devices you add and lists the rest as new.
data_description.ping_interval: How often tracked devices are pinged.

error.invalid_subnet: That is not a valid IPv4 subnet.
error.subnet_too_large: That subnet is too large. Use /22 or smaller.
error.invalid_ip: That is not a valid IP address.
error.gateway_outside: The router IP has to be inside the subnet.

abort.already_configured: This subnet is already set up.

data.auto_hubs: Add hubs automatically when NetOrbit is sure
data.group_by_type: Group devices by type when the layout is unknown
data.snmp_enabled: Read MAC tables from managed switches (SNMP)

data_description.discovery_interval: How often the whole subnet is swept for new devices.
data_description.stale_hours: A device that has not answered for this long turns red and fires a netorbit_device_stale event.
data_description.ignore_random_mac: Phones and laptops often use a private address per network. Leave this on to keep them off the map.
data_description.auto_hubs: When off, everything NetOrbit finds is listed under Review suggested hubs instead.
data_description.group_by_type: On networks where nothing reports which access point a device uses, the card groups devices into TVs, computers, smart home and so on.
data_description.snmp_enabled: NetOrbit asks each device once an hour whether it is a managed switch, using read-only SNMP, then reads the switch's MAC table to place devices automatically.
data_description.snmp_community: Leave empty to try the factory default. If you changed your switches' read-only community, enter it here.
